thread.title: Tesla Stock Might Be Stuck in Place While Elon Musk Stays Mum About Going Private

author: Teresa Rivas
title: Tesla Stock Might Be Stuck in Place While Elon Musk Stays Mum About Going Private
text:
By Teresa Rivas Aug. 21, 2018 1:16 p.m. ET Shares of Tesla (TSLA) are higher on Tuesday, shrugging off a downgrade to Equalweight from Consumer Edge Research.
Where we were: Where to start? A sampling from Tesla's recent wild ride includes a post-earnings pop, go-private tweet , and government investigation , among others.
Where we're headed: Consumer Edge Research warns that the shares could be boxed in until we get more information to evaluate the probability of the shares going private, and Tesla needs to prove that its "fundamentals are sound."
Illustration: Spencer Platt/Getty Images Tesla (TSLA) is climbing higher on Tuesday, a day with little in the way of news or detail about the company's go-private saga, which includes the Securities and Exchange Commission and Saudi Arabia .
However we did get one downgrade today, from Consumer Edge Research 's James Albertine. He cut his rating on the shares to Equalweight from Overweight, with a $311 price target, down from $385 previously, writing that at the moment there are too may variables surrounding the go-private plan.
He cites the ongoing SEC probe, along with questions about CEO Elon Musk 's ability to continue serving in such a "broad capacity" (and without much sleep )–two factors that are "integral" to the stock's near-term price–as evidence that Tesla shares will be rangebound. Add to that that the company may need a "deeper corporate restructuring" and it's hard to see how the stock will break out.
Albertine still believes that Musk is a " generational visionary who has broken new ground by disrupting the 100-plus year-old auto industry," and he's not the only fan of the controversial Tesla CEO . Yet his bad-boy antics, and "inability to maintain his composure" (the abrupt first-quarter earnings conference call now seems tame, given recent developments) shows he has " gone too far ."
Moreover, the analyst argues that while he's optimistic about Model 3 production, he argues that the company needs to prove its "the financial sustainability of its business vision" matches its groundbreaking electric vehicle framework, as well as demonstrating some resolution around the government probe and Musk's role.
"Looking back, there were many times it made sense to sell shares of Amazon.com (AMZN) or Apple (AAPL), for example, despite their meteoric rise and now nearly $2 trillion in collective market capitalization," he concludes. "We believe this may be a similar moment for Tesla [as] management and the board of directors need to pause and regroup through a period of introspection and internal evaluation in order to push forward, ensuring the corporate foundation is suitable to support Tesla’s most ambitious, global, long-term goals."
Shares of Tesla are up 3.9% to $320.30 in afternoon trading.
